Abstract
The precise quantification of corn seedlings is of considerable importance for evaluating planting density, yield estimation, 
and implementing precision agricultural management. Nevertheless, objects frequently exhibit high spatial density in field 
environments, are subject to occlusions, and are affected by complex background interference. Furthermore, edge-computing 
devices are constrained by limited computational resources and energy capacity, making it challenging for traditional mod-
els to achieve accuracy and real-time performance simultaneously. To address this, this paper proposes a lightweight corn 
seedling detection model, YOLO11-SPE, and constructs a drone image dataset for evaluation, based on diverse scenes and 
a specialized occlusion subset. The model is optimized based on YOLO11n with three key improvements: (1) StarNet is 
employed as the lightweight backbone, utilizing element-wise multiplication to enhance nonlinear channel interactions, 
thereby improving the separation of occlusions and edge adhesion; (2) C3k2_PC is introduced at the network neck, incor-
porating pooled token mixing and gated channel modeling to strengthen multi-scale and contextual representations, while 
suppressing false targets; (3) an EfficientHead module is designed, combining decoupled prediction, distributed focal loss 
(DFL), and anchor-free decoding strategies to enhance the localization stability of dense small targets and occluded areas. 
Experimental results show that YOLO11-SPE maintains a relatively stable mAP@0.5 while reducing the model’s parameters, 
FLOPs, and size by approximately 43%, 46%, and 42%, respectively, with an inference speed of 98.9 FPS. In the counting 
regression task, the MAE and RMSE are 4.51 and 6.13, respectively, with an R2 value of 0.9807. This study also conducted 
edge-computing device deployment testing on the Jetson Nano, achieving 24.8 FPS, which is sufficient to meet real-time 
detection requirements.
Keywords  Corn seedling detection · Object counting · Lightweight model · YOLO · Agricultural intelligence
1  Introduction
As an important field crop, corn has its yield significantly 
affected by seedling density. Traditional manual counting 
methods are inefficient, costly, and prone to human error, 
which limits their application in precision agriculture. With 
the development of intelligent algorithms, image-based auto-
matic counting methods can effectively improve efficiency 
and accuracy, driving agricultural production towards intel-
ligence and precision.
Image processing and deep learning-based automatic 
crop counting methods have been widely applied in recent 
years. For example, Veramendi et al. [1] proposed a corn 
plant counting method based on multispectral UAV imagery: 
canopy centers are extracted via thresholding and a distance 
transform, and an SVM [2] classifier is then used for emer-
gence-stage counting and phenological stage recognition, 
achieving a counting accuracy of 88.47% with R2 = 0.98. 
Yu et al. [3] proposed PodNet, which couples a CSPDark-
net backbone with an AFPN [4] neck to fuse small-object 
features efficiently. While maintaining detection accuracy 
with ­R2=0.95, the parameter count is compressed to 2.48 
M, improving real-time performance and deployment effi-
ciency. Shahid et al. [5] developed a tobacco seedling count-
ing framework based on YOLOv7 and SORT [6], providing

emergence through high-precision video-level estimation 
without orthomosaics. Estrada et al. [7] proposed a deep 
learning-based flower-counting method that uses a YOLO 
model and a multicolumn convolutional neural network to 
predict density maps. The method achieved good results in 
high-density peach tree flower counting, with a mean abso-
lute error (MAE) of 39.13, root-mean-square error (RMSE) 
of 69.69, and a percentage error of 9.98%.
In object detection, YOLO[8] series models have been 
widely applied to agricultural crop recognition and detec-
tion due to their superior real-time performance and high 
accuracy. Li et al. [9] proposed Pineapple-YOLO (based 
on YOLOv7-tiny), achieving an mAP@0.5 of 89.7% under 
complex field conditions; Zhu et al. [10] designed YOLO-
LM, which integrates attention mechanisms and multi-fea-
ture fusion, attaining 93.18% accuracy in detecting Camellia 
oleifera (oil-tea) fruits. Wang et al. [11] proposed Insect-
YOLO, which incorporates the CBAM attention module 
to strengthen feature extraction, achieving an mAP@0.5 
of 93.8% in crop insect detection and markedly improving 
small-object recognition performance.
To further meet the requirements of edge deployment, 
researchers have continually optimized model architectures 
to reduce parameter footprint and computational over-
head. Li et al. [12] proposed YOLO11-LES, which jointly 
optimizes LAWDS, EIEStem, and SEAMHead to balance 
detection accuracy and model compactness under occlusion, 
making it suitable for real-time on-device deployment. Zang 
et al. [13] developed the LMDNet model, which incorpo-
rates spatial-channel difference convolution and a Global-
Enhanced Mamba [14] layer to compress the parameter 
count and computational load of an infrared small target 
detection model to only 0.024M and 0.168G, respectively, 
while achieving 41 FPS for real-time inference on edge 
devices, significantly enhancing its deployment applicabil-
ity. Umirzakova et al. [22] proposed the CMTL framework, 
which employs a context modeling approach through a 
cross-layer multi-granularity encoder (CLMGE) and multi-
task self-distillation attention fusion (MSDAF), effectively 
integrating information from different tasks and enhancing 
the accuracy and efficiency of cotton boll detection, pest 
segmentation, and phenological stage classification. This 
makes it particularly suitable for real-time deployment on 
edge devices.
Although existing methods have made significant pro-
gress in crop detection and counting tasks, the balance 
between accuracy and lightweight performance has yet to 
be fully achieved in the complex field environments of corn 
seedling detection, where small target density, occlusion, 
and background interference pose challenges. Existing mod-
els typically increase computational overhead and model 
size while improving accuracy, which presents challenges 
for real-time processing and edge device [16] deployment. 
Therefore, reducing computational burden and model size 
while maintaining high accuracy remains an issue that needs 
to be addressed.
To address the occlusion issue in corn seedling detection, 
this paper proposes a lightweight improved YOLO11-SPE 
model based on the YOLO11n architecture. By integrat-
ing the StarNet backbone, C3k2_PC encoding module, and 
EfficientHead detection head, the model enhances feature 
extraction capabilities, optimizes small target perception and 
regression accuracy, while significantly reducing the model 
size.
In addition, this paper constructs a high-density corn 
seedling detection dataset consisting of 1,004 drone-cap-
tured images and 96,417 target instances. The dataset covers 
various complex field interference factors such as weeds, 
shadows, film reflection, and seedling occlusion, providing 
a solid foundation for evaluating and validating the model’s 
generalization capability. Specifically, a subset contain-
ing 209 images with heavy occlusion is created to further 
investigate the model’s adaptability under complex occlu-
sion conditions.
Experimental results show that YOLO11-SPE main-
tains a relatively stable detection accuracy while reducing 
the model’s parameters, computational load, and size by 
approximately 43%, 46%, and 42%, respectively. The MAE 
and RMSE decrease by 14.3% and 14.2%, respectively, with 
the R2 value rising to 0.9807, demonstrating superior count-
ing performance and adaptability for edge deployment. Spe-
cifically, YOLO11-SPE outperforms the baseline model for 
the heavily occluded subset in terms of MAE and RMSE, 
indicating its ability to maintain stable performance even in 
seedling overlap and boundary blurring cases. This verifies 
the practical application value of the proposed method in 
corn seedling dense counting scenarios.
2  Dataset construction
2.1  Image collection
Data were collected from corn fields in Etuoke Qianqi, 
Ordos, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, using a DJI 
Mavic UAV flown at 3–7 m above ground level, with the 
gimbal fixed at a 90◦ nadir orientation. The collection took 
place from May to June 2025, daily from 09:00 to 11:00 
and 15:00 to 17:00, covering diverse illumination condi-
tions (intense, low, and shadows). Sampling spanned from 
emergence to the four-leaf stage to ensure morphological 
diversity and scene representativeness. Illustrative growth 
stages are shown in Fig. 1.
A total of 1,004 corn seedling images were collected at 
resolutions of 2048×2048 and 3840×2160 in JPG format.

adaptability to occlusions.
2.2  Data annotation and data augmentation
This study uses a YOLO-format dataset, with corn seed-
lings manually annotated in the images using the LabelImg 
tool. The annotation process strictly defines the bounding 
boxes of the seedlings based on their actual morphological 
characteristics at the seedling stage, ensuring high-quality 
data labeling.
To improve the model’s convergence speed and generali-
zation ability, and enhance its robustness to complex field 
environments, this study designed five data augmentation 
strategies: Gaussian blur, brightness-contrast adjustment, 
color saturation adjustment, affine transformation, and 
local random occlusion. These augmentation methods are 
randomly combined to address various complex scenarios in 
corn seedling detection, such as different lighting conditions, 
occlusions, cluttered backgrounds, and angle variations. For

3  Research methodology
3.1  YOLO11 detection model
YOLO11, as the latest evolution of the YOLO series single-
stage object detection framework, achieves a breakthrough 
balance between accuracy and efficiency through multi-level 
structural innovations. The model follows the classic four-
level modular design: the input module employs adaptive 
image scaling technology and standardized preprocess-
ing, dynamically accommodating input data of different 
resolutions; the backbone network is based on depthwise 
separable convolutions and a cross-stage local architecture 
(CSPNet [17]) to construct a multi-scale feature extraction 
system. The core improvement lies in replacing YOLOv8’s 
C2f module with a gradient-optimized C3k2 [18] module. 
While retaining the multi-branch gradient reuse feature 
reduces redundant computation layers by restructuring the 
feature propagation path, it significantly lowers the number 
of parameters and computational overhead. The neck struc-
ture innovatively integrates the C3k2 module, upsampling 
operations, and cross-layer feature concatenation (Concat) 
mechanism. Compared to YOLOv8’s basic feature pyramid 
design, a new C2PSA dual-path attention module is added, 
which selects key feature channels along the channel dimen-
sion and focuses on target salient areas along the spatial 
dimension, effectively enhancing feature discrimination in 
complex backgrounds. The detection head adopts a decou-
pled design paradigm, processing object classification and 
bounding box regression tasks through independent branches 
in parallel. Two additional depthwise separable convolution 
layers are introduced in the classification branch to optimize 
the feature refinement process, a design that YOLOv8 lacks.
YOLO11 officially provides five versions of object detec-
tion weights: n, s, m, l, and x, with model complexity and 
accuracy increasing progressively (parameter count ranging 
from 2.6M to 56.9M). Considering edge devices’ limited 
computational resources and the importance of detection 
speed, this study selects the lightweight YOLO11n as the 
baseline model.

3.2  YOLO11‑SPE detection model
This study addresses the target occlusion problem in corn 
seedling automatic counting tasks under field conditions. 
Corn seedlings are typically densely distributed and often 
accompanied by complex backgrounds (such as soil, weeds, 
and crop residue) and lighting variations, making misde-
tections and missed detections due to occlusion a common 
issue. Therefore, the detection model must have strong fea-
ture extraction and occluded target recognition capabilities 
while improving detection accuracy and inference speed. 
To facilitate deployment on edge devices with limited com-
putational resources, the model must minimize parameter 
count and computational complexity while maintaining high 
performance, ensuring its lightweight characteristics.
To address this, an improved YOLO11-SPE corn seedling 
detection model is designed. The backbone adopts StarNet 
[21], which introduces element-wise multiplication (star) to 
expand the implicit feature expression space without sig-
nificantly increasing channel width or computational load. 
This enhances the model’s ability to separate boundary 
adhesion and local occlusions, and improves the detection 
rate of small targets, while maintaining a lightweight struc-
ture suitable for edge deployment. The backbone further 
integrates SPPF (Spatial Pyramid Pooling Fast) and C2PSA 
(Channel-Spatial Attention) to strengthen multi-scale and 
spatial-context modeling, providing more robust perception 
for partially occluded seedlings. In terms of the neck and 
detection head, the C3k2_PC module [22] is proposed: it 
introduces pooled token mixing [15] and Gated Linear Units 
(CGLU [19]) under the CSP framework, using “local context 
smoothing + token-wise channel gating” to suppress false 
targets such as reflections and weeds, alleviating misdetec-
tions and missed detections caused by dense occlusions and 
boundary adhesions. A customized EfficientHead is also 
designed, using lightweight decoupled branches and dis-
tributed focal loss (DFL) combined with anchor-free [20] 
decoding to improve localization stability and prediction 
quality in occluded, overlapping, and dense small target 
areas. The structure of the improved YOLO11-SPE model 
is shown in Fig. 4.

To further optimize feature extraction capabilities, Star-
Net employs depthwise convolution (DWConv) for initial 
feature extraction. Compared to traditional convolution oper-
ations, depthwise convolution decomposes the convolution 
process by performing independent convolutions on each 
input channel, then summing the results element-wise. This 
significantly reduces the number of parameters and com-
putational complexity, thereby improving both training and 
inference efficiency.
Thanks to depthwise separable convolutions and a com-
pact stage design, StarNet controls the backbone capacity 
while providing sufficient receptive field and discriminative 
power. Combined with the feature fusion and detection head 
optimizations proposed in this study, it effectively reduces 
parameter count and FLOPs while ensuring real-time per-
formance, enabling stable operation across various edge 
hardware platforms, such as GPU, CPU, and NPU.
3.2.2  Design of the C3k2_PC module and lightweight 
feature modeling mechanism
To balance the dense occlusion of seedlings and the effi-
ciency constraints of edge deployment, this paper builds the 
C3k2_PC module on the C3k2 primitive of YOLO11. Its 
structure, shown in Fig. 6, follows the MetaFormer para-
digm: Token Mixer (Pooling) → Channel Mixer (CGLU) 
→ Residual. The core idea is to inject stable local context 
and suppress noise via zero-parameter pooling-based token 
mixing, followed by fine-grained selection along the chan-
nel dimension using a Convolutional Gated Linear Unit 
(CGLU). This design reduces parameter count and com-
putational overhead while enhancing discriminability in 
occluded regions and stabilizing counting performance.
Token Mixing (Pooling): For each location in the feature 
map, perform mean aggregation over a local window and 
subtract the original value at that location, thereby inject-
ing local spatial context at negligible cost and suppressing 
high-frequency spurious patterns such as specular reflections 
and soil textures. Formally, 
where K denotes the window size, the computational com-
plexity of this design scales linearly with spatial resolution, 
enabling efficient inference on high-resolution feature maps; 
when coupled with normalization applied jointly over (C, 
H, W), it further stabilizes deep training and multi-scale 
distributions.
Channel Mixing (CGLU) adopts a “value branch × 
gating branch” structure. The input is projected by a 
1 × 1 convolution to form the value branch; in parallel, 
the gating branch applies a 1 × 1 projection followed by a 
lightweight 3 × 3 depthwise convolution to inject a local 
positional prior. After a nonlinear activation, the result-
ing gating coefficients are applied to the value branch 
via element-wise multiplication, and a final 1 × 1 pro-
jection restores the channel dimensionality. This token-
wise, fine-grained gating preserves class-relevant chan-
nel responses in overlapping or adherent regions while 
incurring minimal computational overhead, achieving a 
better balance between accuracy and efficiency than con-
ventional convolutional feed-forward designs.
C3k2_PC establishes a coarse-to-fine, lightweight dis-
criminative pathway: an initial pooling-based token mixer 
builds a stable local context and denoising base, followed 
by gated channel selection that selectively amplifies or 
suppresses features, jointly improving robustness to 
densely occluded regions and spurious targets. Coupled 
with a multi-scale feature pyramid, it further reduces 
merged-instance false positives and counting fluctuations 
without increasing inference overhead, thereby enhancing 
edge deployability.
3.2.3  Design and lightweight optimization 
of the efficienthead detection head
To improve the inference efficiency and structural com-
pactness of object detection models, this paper proposes 
the EfficientHead detection head module. This module 
optimizes the traditional YOLO series detection head to 
reduce parameter count and computational overhead while 
maintaining high accuracy, enhancing the model’s deploy-
ment capability on edge devices.
EfficientHead reduces computational load by introduc-
ing two layers of 3 × 3 group convolutions and adopts a 
decoupled design to separate the regression and classifica-
tion tasks, minimizing interference between tasks. In the 
regression branch, the Distributed Focal Loss (DFL) mech-

4  Experimental results and analysis
4.1  Experimental environment and hyperparameter 
configuration
This study was implemented using the PyTorch deep learn-
ing framework within an Anaconda virtual environment. The 
experimental setup and hyperparameter settings are sum-
marized in Tables 1 and 2.
4.2  Evaluation metrics
To comprehensively evaluate YOLO11-SPE on corn seed-
ling images, we define metrics at two levels: object detection 
accuracy and image-level counting error.
4.2.1  Detection performance metrics
We evaluate localization performance using Precision, 
Recall, and mean Average Precision (mAP@0.5). Precision 
measures the proportion of predicted corn seedling instances 
that are correct; Recall measures the proportion of all true 
seedlings that are successfully detected; mAP@0.5 denotes 
the mean average precision at an IoU threshold of 0.5, 
reflecting the model’s overall detection capability:
In the equations, TP (true positive) denotes the number of 
instances predicted as positive that are actually positive; FP 
(false positive) denotes the number of instances predicted as 
positive but actually negative; FN (false negative) denotes 
the number of instances predicted as negative but actually 
positive.
4.2.2  Counting error metrics
Counting performance is assessed using mean absolute error 
(MAE), root-mean-square error (RMSE), and the coefficient 
of determination ( R2 ). MAE quantifies the average deviation 
between predicted and ground-truth counts; RMSE penalizes 
larger deviations and, when smaller, indicates more precise 
counting; R2 measures goodness of fit between predictions 
and ground truth, with values closer to 1 indicating better fit.
To address potential risks in agricultural applications, 
such as pesticide dosage control, agricultural decision-
making often follows the principle of “better to over-detect 
than to miss a detection.” Therefore, a lower threshold was 
selected for the counting performance test in this study:

4.8  Comparison experiment
To evaluate the comprehensive performance of YOLO11-
SPE, comparisons were conducted against YOLOv5n, 
YOLOv8n, YOLOv10n, YOLOv9-t, YOLO11n and 
YOLOv13n (see Table  8). YOLO11-SPE achieves the

to 0.973, the model complexity is substantially optimized: 
parameters reduced to 1.47M, computation to 3.4 GFLOPs, 
and model size to 3.2 MB—corresponding to reductions of 
approximately 43%, 46%, and 42%, respectively—with an 
inference speed of 98.9 FPS. Taken together, YOLO11-SPE 
markedly improves lightweightness and inference efficiency 
while maintaining accuracy, making it suitable for real-time 
seedling monitoring and dense crop counting in agricultural 
scenarios.
5  Conclusion
This study addresses the need for automatic detection and 
counting of corn seedlings in high-density and occluded 
environments by proposing the lightweight detection model 
YOLO11-SPE. By integrating the StarNet backbone, C3k2_
PC module, and EfficientHead detection head, the model 
enhances feature extraction, regression accuracy, and small 
target detection capabilities. Maintaining inference speed 
and computational efficiency significantly improves the 
discriminative power and stability in occluded, dense scenes.
The experimental results show that YOLO11-SPE reduces 
the parameter count, computational load, and model size by 
approximately 43%, 46%, and 42%, respectively, with an 
inference speed of 98.9 FPS. It maintains strong regression 
performance, with MAE reduced to 4.51, RMSE at 6.13, 
and R2 improved to 0.9807, demonstrating its advantages 
in corn seedling counting tasks. In addition, deployment on 
edge-computing devices has validated its outstanding real-
time performance and edge-computing capabilities. At the 
same time, it retains strong robustness and generalization in 
highly occluded and high-density areas, making it suitable 
for intelligent agricultural scenarios such as seed quality 
evaluation, yield prediction, and seedling monitoring, with 
high practical value and broad application potential.
Although YOLO11-SPE performs excellently in many 
areas, there is still room for improvement. Currently, the 
training primarily uses fixed scales and data from specific 
plots and single crop varieties. Further improvements are 
needed for generalization to ultra-high resolution, cross-
region, and cross-variety scenarios. Future work will con-
tinue to focus on real-world production environments, with a 
priority on expanding data diversity and addressing complex 
occlusion cases, as well as on joint training and inference 
using multi-scale and dynamic-scale approaches.

Abstract: The precise quantification of corn seedlings is of considerable importance for evaluating planting density, yield estimation, and implementing precision agricultural management. Nevertheless, objects frequently exhibit high spatial density in field environments, are subject to occlusions, and are affected by complex background interference. Furthermore, edge-computing devices are constrained by limited computational resources and energy capacity, making it challenging for traditional mod- els to achieve accuracy and real-time performance simultaneously. To address this, this paper proposes a lightweight corn seedling detection model, YOLO11-SPE, and constructs a drone image dataset for evaluation, based on diverse scenes and a specialized occlusion subset. The model is optimized based on YOLO11n with three key improvements: (1) StarNet is employed as the lightweight backbone, utilizing element-wise multiplication to enhance nonlinear channel interactions, thereby improving the separation of occlusions and edge adhesion; (2) C3k2_PC is introduced at the network neck, incor- porating pooled token mixing and gated channel modeling to strengthen multi-scale and contextual representations, while suppressing false targets; (3) an EfficientHead module is designed, combining decoupled prediction, distributed focal loss (DFL), and anchor-free decoding strategies to enhance the localization stability of dense small targets and occluded areas. Experimental results show that YOLO11-SPE maintains a relatively stable mAP@0.5 while reducing the model’s parameters, FLOPs, and size by approximately 43%, 46%, and 42%, respectively, with an inference speed of 98.9 FPS. In the counting regression task, the MAE and RMSE are 4.51 and 6.13, respectively, with an R2 value of 0.9807. This study also conducted edge-computing device deployment testing on the Jetson Nano, achieving 24.8 FPS, which is sufficient to meet real-time detection requirements.
